newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bank BOS IPO seen oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: Polish bank BOS IPO seen oversubscribed.

text.p: The 1.2-million-share initial public offering of Poland's Bank Ochrony Srodowiska SA (BOS), which ends on Thursday, is likely to be oversubscribed, the deputy president of the bank said on Wednesday.
"In the large investor tranche we've had an oversubscription and the offering for small investors has not yet been finished, but we expect an oversubscription as well," Jerzy Pietrewicz told Reuters.
He said the final results of the issue, priced at 29 zlotys per share, would be announced on November 6.
The bank, which seeks a main market listing in January 1997, last week offered 800,000 shares to large investors, who could register for at least 25,000 shares.
In the small investor tranche, which ends on Thursday, the bank is offering 400,000 shares.
BOS, which specialises in funding environmental protection projects, had a net profit of 31.8 million zlotys in 1995 on 210.6 million zlotys in interest and other related revenues.
The bank's main shareholders are the National Fund for Environmental Protection and Water Management, with 44.4 percent, the State Treasury, with 7.8 percent, and Ciech SA with 5.8 percent.
